title: pvDecimate
body:
## pvDecimate

Reduces the triangle count of a triangle surface with vtkDecimatePro, removing vertices in order of least error until TargetReduction (ParaView default 0.9, about 90 % of triangles removed) is reached. By ParaView default PreserveTopology is off, so the surface may be split along feature edges (FeatureAngle 15°) and holes may open to reach the target. Input must be triangles; run triangulate first. decimate is the curated version (Schemaxis defaults 0.5, topology preserved); pvQuadricClustering is faster on very large meshes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The native defaults remove 90 % of triangles and allow holes; set PreserveTopology true and a smaller TargetReduction when the surface must stay closed.
- Only triangles are processed; triangulate general polygons first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Decimate`. Identity: `filters/DecimatePro`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Decimate filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BoundaryVertexDeletion` | If this property is set to 1, then vertices on the boundary of the dataset can be removed. Setting the value of this property to 0 preserves the boundary of the dataset, but it may cause the filter not to reach its reduction target. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FeatureAngle` | The value of this property is used in determining where the data set may be split. If the angle between two adjacent triangles is greater than or equal to the FeatureAngle value, then their boundary is considered a feature edge where the dataset can be split. | `{"maximum":180.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `PreserveTopology` | If this property is set to 1, decimation will not split the dataset or produce holes, but it may keep the filter from reaching the reduction target. If it is set to 0, better reduction can occur (reaching the reduction target), but holes in the model may be produced. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `TargetReduction` | This property specifies the desired reduction in the total number of polygons in the output dataset. For example, if the TargetReduction value is 0.9, the Decimate filter will attempt to produce an output dataset that is 10% the size of the input.) | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json

  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvDecimate",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
